answer: Each agent earns trust through a kernel that releases payment only after independently verified work, while quill records bind each claim to a costly, nontransferable stake. A reviewer chosen at random checks the result against a public task; a false claim forfeits the stake and lowers the identities’ future limits. Splitting one operator across many names therefore multiplies the capital locked in each quill and risks repeated losses, while an opal badge alone buys no influence.
